title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 352
paragraphs: and after him reigned a blind man from the city of Anysis, whose name was Anysis. In his reign the Ethiopians, led by their king Sabacos, marched against Egypt with a great host. So this blind man fled and took refuge in the marshlands, and the Ethiopian ruled over Egypt for fifty years, during which he did the following: whenever an Egyptian committed a transgression, he would never put him to death, but he sentenced each man according to the gravity of the offense, ordering them to throw up an embankment before the city each offender came from. In this way the cities were raised still higher than before; for they had first been embanked by those who dug the channels in the reign of Sesostris, and then again in the reign of the Ethiopian, and so they were raised very high. While other cities in Egypt also stood high, I think it was at Bubastis in particular that the earth was piled up most. In this city there is a temple very much worth mentioning, for though there are other larger and more costly temples, none is more pleasing to the eye than this one.
